Constantīnopolis, Constantīnopolis f.

noun, third declension

A town takes no preposition: Constantīnopolim (to), Constantīnopolī (at), Constantīnopolī (from). The name from the fourth century; the older Greek city was Bȳzantium.

Other words

  • Bȳzantium, Bȳzantiī n. — the city before Constantine, Byzantium

    noun, second declension · classical · Mel. 2.2.6 (Lewis & Short); Plin. 4.46 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 38.16.3 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. Istanbul, Constantinople (Tursellinus 1652)

    The ancient Greek city on the Bosporus; Constantīnopolis is its later name, after Constantine (Lewis & Short).

  • Constantīnopolītānus, Constantīnopolītāna, Constantīnopolītānum — of Constantinople

    declension · late Latin · M-O s.v. Turkey cities: Istanbul (Cod. Just.); Cod. Just. 1.2.6 (Lewis & Short s.v. Constantinopolis)

See also Asia Minor, Turkey, Bosporus.
